# PyAutoCTI Assistant

> The front door of the PyAutoCTI Assistant — an AI assistant for Charge Transfer Inefficiency (CTI) calibration and correction with PyAutoCTI: agent instructions, task skills and a reference wiki in one repository that you drive in natural language from inside an AI coding agent. It routes by intent: set up, see what the assistant can do, read the reference, or jump to runnable examples.

## How to use it

The assistant is supported **only inside an AI coding agent** that can read this repository and execute Python: **Claude Code** or **Codex** (recommended and tested), or **OpenCode** as an experimental alternative. Clone the repository and open the agent inside it — `AGENTS.md` (via `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code) loads automatically:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autocti_assistant.git
cd autocti_assistant
claude        # or: codex / opencode
```

Then paste the starting prompt from the [README](./README.md). Desktop and IDE versions of these agents are fine when they provide the same repository and execution access. Browser chats with a GitHub connector are **not supported**: they cannot run the arctic-backed stack or inspect data, which the assistant's safeguards depend on.

Agentic does not mean autonomous: you can ask what CTI is, plan a calibration or learn in **Teacher Mode** without running anything — say so in your prompt.

## If you are an agent reading this file

Read order: [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) → [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md) → the relevant skill → [wiki/](./wiki). Never write PyAutoCTI from memory: mirror the matching skill or a `scripts/demonstrations/` script and verify symbols against the installed library (`dir()`, or `python autoassistant/audit_skill_apis.py --code "<snippet>"` on a harness without the PreToolUse code gate). Inspect real data before composing any fit; if you cannot execute code in this session, ask the user to and report back — the gate is never waived.

## Agent instructions (canonical)

- [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md): safety rules, modes, and repository conventions — the source of truth.

## What it can do

- [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md): one-line index of every task skill. This cell was born as a lightweight seed; [PENDING.md](./PENDING.md) is the growth queue.

## Reference

- [wiki/core/index.md](./wiki/core/index.md): curated CTI + PyAuto* reference — what CTI is, trap physics, FPR/EPER, the arctic algorithm, calibration strategy.
- [wiki/literature/index.md](./wiki/literature/index.md): CTI science wiki — detector physics, correction algorithms, Euclid VIS / HST ACS, trap pumping, CTI as a weak-lensing systematic; verified bibliography.

## Runnable examples & tutorials (elsewhere)

- [autocti_workspace](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autocti_workspace): end-to-end example scripts and notebooks (no llms.txt routing layer yet — browse `scripts/` directly).
- `scripts/demonstrations/` (in this repo): four runnable end-to-end demos — calibrate a 1D dataset and a charge-injection image (recovering the input traps), correct CTI, and load results through the aggregator.
